headline: 445 earthquake-safe shelters identified in Dhaka to protect residents
summary: Disaster Management Minister Asadul Habib Dulu announced the initiative in parliament, including the training of 100,000 volunteers for emergency response.
details: The government has identified 445 safe shelters across Dhaka to protect residents during earthquakes and other emergencies, according to Disaster Management Minister Asadul Habib Dulu.
A proposal has been sent to the Prime Minister’s Office to formally designate these locations as ‘earthquake-safe shelters’.
Of the total, 256 shelters are located in Dhaka South City Corporation and 189 are in Dhaka North City Corporation.
To strengthen rescue and emergency response, the government is preparing 100,000 volunteers in Dhaka and surrounding areas.
Coordination between the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, the Geological Survey Department, and other agencies has been improved for faster dissemination of earthquake and tsunami warnings.
Minister Dulu emphasized that Bangladesh's proximity to vulnerable regions makes disaster preparedness a high priority for the government.
The minister also stressed the importance of adhering to the Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) to ensure the construction of earthquake-resistant infrastructure.
caption:
Dhaka is getting 445 designated earthquake-safe shelters to protect its residents during emergencies.

Of the total, 256 shelters are located in Dhaka South City Corporation and 189 are in Dhaka North City Corporation.

To strengthen rescue and emergency response, the government is preparing 100,000 volunteers in Dhaka and surrounding areas.

Coordination between the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, the Geological Survey Department, and other agencies has been improved for faster dissemination of earthquake and tsunami warnings.

Minister Dulu emphasized that Bangladesh's proximity to vulnerable regions makes disaster preparedness a high priority for the government.

The minister also stressed the importance of adhering to the Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) to ensure the construction of earthquake-resistant infrastructure.

headline: Jagannath University student Sirajul remains missing for 5 days
summary: Efforts are underway to form a 'Quick Response Team' to locate the missing sociology student.
details: Sirajul, a student of Jagannath University, has been missing for five days, causing deep concern among his family and peers.
Despite various efforts to locate him, no information regarding his whereabouts has been found so far.
In response to the disappearance, there are initiatives to form a 'Quick Response Team' to accelerate the search process.
The university community and family are hopeful that the student will be found safely and soon.
caption:
A Jagannath University student has been missing for five days with no leads on his whereabouts.

Sirajul, a student of Jagannath University, has been missing for five days, causing deep concern among his family and peers.

Despite various efforts to locate him, no information regarding his whereabouts has been found so far.

In response to the disappearance, there are initiatives to form a 'Quick Response Team' to accelerate the search process.

The university community and family are hopeful that the student will be found safely and soon.
